method: Direct HTTP GET requests via curl against the Docker Hub v2 public API and the ghcr.io anonymous-token endpoint, executed on 2026-08-14, with raw JSON responses parsed programmatically (not summarized by an intermediate LLM step) for the registry facts; the deployment-guide quotes were retrieved via web fetch of the live docs page.
limitations: Docker Hub's search API and namespace listing are complete for the 'prisma' and 'prismagraphql' namespaces as queried, but a name-based search cannot prove the total absence of a relevant image outside those namespaces (e.g. under an unrelated org name); this is a bounded-search limitation, not a guarantee of exhaustiveness. The ghcr.io check only tested three plausible image-path guesses (prisma/prisma, prisma/prisma-cli, prisma/engines) under the 'prisma' GitHub-org namespace; GitHub Packages listing via the authenticated API (api.github.com/orgs/prisma/packages) returned 401 Unauthorized because it requires an access token this research did not use, so a definitive enumerated list of all ghcr.io packages published by the prisma org could not be obtained — recorded as a gap, not as proof of absence. No Docker image was pulled or run, per task boundary.
provenance: Registry facts are re-verifiable by re-issuing the same curl commands against the same public API endpoints (no authentication required for Docker Hub search/listing; ghcr.io anonymous-token probe also requires no credentials). The deployment guide is re-verifiable by visiting the URL in raw_evidence[].url directly.

official_docker_image_availability.citation: Docker Hub namespace listing for 'prismagraphql' (last_updated 2019-11-11T10:27:59Z for the 'prisma' repo); ghcr.io token-endpoint 403s for the three most plausible current-org image paths; Prisma's own Docker deployment guide, section 3
official_docker_image_availability.rationale: No currently-maintained, officially-published Prisma CLI/engines Docker image was found on either public registry checked. The only Docker Hub image plausibly named for the current product, prismagraphql/prisma, was last updated 2019-11-11 — this is Prisma 1, the deprecated GraphQL-server product that predates the schema.prisma-based Prisma ORM (Prisma 2+) this survey is about; it is a different product under a legacy namespace, not the candidate in scope, and using it would be a category error. The other prismagraphql/* repositories with recent (2026-03-06) activity (build, mongo-single-replica, cockroachdb-custom) are internal CI/test-fixture images (a build image and seeded-database images for running Prisma's own integration test suite), not a published CLI or engines product image for end users. ghcr.io returned 403 (not merely 404) for the three most plausible current image paths under the prisma org, consistent with — though not conclusive proof of — no public image existing at those paths; a full, authenticated enumeration of the org's ghcr.io packages was not performed (see limitations). The docs' own deployment guide confirms the officially recommended path is NOT a dedicated Prisma image: it instructs building a Dockerfile FROM a generic node:alpine or node:slim base image and running `npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma generate` inside it. This is materially different from factory/scripts/structurizr's pattern of pulling one official, versioned image and invoking a validate/export-svg/export-png subcommand — there is no equivalent single official image to pull for Prisma; a project would have to build and maintain its own Dockerfile around the node base image and npx invocations.

This is a materially different, and weaker, answer than 'an official image exists at tag X' — recorded exactly as such per the task's explicit instruction not to accept a README/blog claim in place of a registry-listing check, and not to substitute the npx-in-generic-image path for a genuine official image without saying so.
